short: The six human SIX genes encode homeodomain proteins with an additional SIX domain that recruits the EYA family of transcriptional coactivators. Their shared DNA core is TGATAC (GTATCA on the other strand), usually embedded in a longer element written GTAACCTGATAC, which on the opposite strand contains the MEF3 site TCAGGTT first defined in the myogenin promoter. SIX1, SIX2 and SIX4 partner with EYA proteins and activate transcription; SIX3 and SIX6 instead recruit Groucho/TLE corepressors and repress. The family builds muscle, kidney, inner ear and eye: SIX1 mutations cause branchio-oto-renal syndrome, SIX3 mutations cause holoprosencephaly, and SIX1 with EYA is re-activated in several carcinomas.
long:
## The factors

Six human genes - SIX1, SIX2, SIX3, SIX4, SIX5 and SIX6 - encode the vertebrate relatives of *Drosophila* sine oculis. Each protein carries a homeodomain preceded by a roughly 110-residue SIX domain, which is the family's second functional module: it does not bind DNA but provides the interaction surface for the EYA coactivators, and the crystal structure of the human SIX1 SIX domain bound to the EYA2 ED domain shows how that interface is organized. The family splits on cofactor use rather than on sequence. SIX1, SIX2 and SIX4 bind EYA1-4; EYA has intrinsic protein tyrosine phosphatase activity and its recruitment converts a SIX-DACH complex from repressing to activating, so the same site can give opposite outputs depending on which partner is present. SIX3 and SIX6 do not bind EYA and instead recruit Groucho-related corepressors through an eh1-like motif in the SIX domain, acting as repressors. SIX1 and SIX4 are expressed in somites, muscle satellite cells, kidney and otic placode; SIX2 in nephron progenitors; SIX3 and SIX6 in the anterior neural plate, retina and hypothalamus. SIX5 is a family member with no motif model in any of the four collections used here.

## The motif

All SIX models in these databases converge on a GATAC core. The HT-SELEX and methyl-SELEX models - SIX1.H14CORE.1.SM.B, SIX2.H14CORE.2.SM.B, SIX3.H14CORE.0.SM.B, SIX6.H14CORE.0.SM.B and two CIS-BP models - reduce to tGATAC, 6-9 bits. The ChIP-derived and longer JASPAR models extend it: SIX1 and SIX2 give tGaAAcyTGAtac, JASPAR SIX1 gives GtAACCTGA, JASPAR SIX2 TGAAACCTGAt, SIX4 TGtAAccTGAcACC, and the Vierstra archetype AC0459 GtAACcTGAta. Read the long version on the opposite strand and the classical name appears: GTAACCTGATAC is GTATCAGGTTAC reversed, and TCAGGTT is the MEF3 motif identified in the myogenin promoter as the site through which Six1 and Six4 activate myogenin during somitogenesis. So the family has one site described under two names and two strand conventions; the pooled consensus here, GtaACgcGATACc, is the long form. Two caveats about the split written into this family's definition. First, SIX3 and SIX6 are sometimes described as preferring a TAAT-type site rather than the MEF3 site, but in these four databases their in vitro models give the same TGATAC core as SIX1/2/4, and the JASPAR Six3 model (AtaGGGTATCA) is the GTATCA form - so the SIX1/2/4 versus SIX3/6 division is a cofactor distinction, not one you can make from sequence. Second, one CIS-BP member of this family reads GAgTTGTAGT and has nearest neighbours among the ETS factors; it should not be used as a SIX motif.

## Where it acts

SIX sites occur in tissue-specific enhancers and promoters: the myogenin promoter MEF3 element, nephron progenitor enhancers for SIX2, otic and branchial arch enhancers for SIX1, and forebrain and retinal enhancers for SIX3 and SIX6. The functional unit is usually a SIX site plus its cofactor complex rather than a cluster of different motifs, which is why composite element names are rare for this family. Because the core is only 6 bp, exact TGATAC matches number on the order of 10^6 genome-wide and carry almost no information alone; the 11-13 bp extended form is far more discriminating. Note that the short models will also match GATA-like sequence by coincidence - one Vierstra archetype in this family is labelled SIX/GATA for that reason.

## Biology and disease

Heterozygous SIX1 mutations cause branchio-oto-renal syndrome by disrupting EYA1-SIX1-DNA complexes, and Six1 or Six4 loss in mouse impairs myogenesis and kidney and inner ear development. SIX2 is required to maintain nephron progenitors. Mutations in the SIX3 homeodomain cause holoprosencephaly, and Six3 represses Wnt signaling in the anterior neuroectoderm, which is required for forebrain formation; SIX6 lies in a chromosome 14 cluster and is associated with eye malformation and, in common variation, with optic disc and glaucoma phenotypes. The SIX1-EYA complex is re-expressed in breast, ovarian and other carcinomas, where it promotes migration and metastasis, and is being pursued as a drug target.

## Reading a hit

A bare TGATAC hit is close to meaningless: 6 bp, high genomic frequency, and shared by every SIX paralogue. Insist on the extended GTAACCTGATAC / MEF3 form before calling a site. Even then the hit identifies the family and not the member, and it does not tell you the output, because SIX1/2/4 with EYA activate while SIX3/6 with Groucho repress at what looks like the same sequence. The SIX1, SIX2 and SIX4 models graded P in HOCOMOCO come from ChIP alone and their 5' extension may reflect co-bound partners; the SM-graded models are the in vitro evidence and are the short GATAC form.
caveats: The GATAC core is only 6 bp and is shared by all SIX paralogues, so short matches are uninformative and will also pick up GATA-like sequence - one Vierstra archetype here is labelled SIX/GATA. Use the extended 11-13 bp MEF3 form. A hit cannot distinguish SIX1, SIX2, SIX3, SIX4 or SIX6, and cannot predict activation versus repression, since that depends on whether EYA or Groucho is recruited. SIX5 has no model here at all. One CIS-BP member of the family reads an ETS-like sequence (GAGTTGTAGT) and is flagged as belonging elsewhere; the longer SIX1/2/4 models are ChIP-derived and may include partner contributions.
